title: Production Agent Runtimes — Fast Instantiation and Typed Workflows
service: AgnoMastra: an Agno-shaped stateless request handler with a fresh agent per request, Mastra-shaped typed tools and workflows, composite storage, a Little's-law capacity planner, an HTTP/1.1 chunked streaming backend and a structural schema checker for nested workflows
runtime: Python 3.10+, standard library, pytest; no network and no LLM: every model is a deterministic function the tests supply

parts.lesson_anchor: Agno: stateless session-scoped FastAPI backend, each request starts a fresh agent, session state lives in a DB, ~2μs instantiation; Mastra: Tools (Zod-typed; code/main.ts checkSchema walks the schema's fields, each one checked for presence, then type), Workflows; code/main.py main() passing one agent to every agno_request_handler call, MastraAgent.run, MastraWorkflow.run
planted_bugs: AgnoApp.__init__ builds one Agent and handle() reuses it for every request (as code/main.py main() passes one agent to every agno_request_handler call), so its memory piles up across requests and session s2 sees session s1
MastraAgent.run records the schema error but has no continue, so the tool still runs; the AttributeError surfaces inside the test's search tool, two calls away

check_input walks the caller's args instead of the schema, so a call that leaves out a required field passes the check and the tool runs, while the docstring asks for 'missing field <key>' and the tool not called; it shows only after the continue is fixed, as a TypeError raised where run calls the test's search tool with no arguments, after check_input, where the cause is, has already returned None. The fix has to keep the schema's order field by field (presence, then type) and tell a None value from a missing field
Agent.__init__ deep-copies the whole tool registry, so instantiation grows with the registry; with one shared agent it is paid once, and it shows only after every request builds its own agent
parts.timing_assert: 300 requests on an app with 1000 tools under 0.05 s. Measured on this machine (Python 3.12, other agents running): deep copy 0.83-1.57 s, 1.96 s under the checker's heaviest load; shared registry 0.14-0.61 ms; a shallow dict copy per agent 1.0-1.2 ms, which the timing cannot catch, so the registry identity check does
parts.overfix_guard: every request must run on a distinct Agent object, which rules out keeping one agent on the app with its memory reset per run, re-caching it to pass the timing, or caching one agent per session; every agent must hold the app's registry object itself, which rules out a shallow copy per agent; Workflow.run already deep-copies each step's output in the starter, and the workflow trace assertions (steps that change the payload in place must not rewrite earlier entries) stay as a guard: dropping that copy along with the registry's deep copy, or making it shallow so nested lists still change, fails there

parts.lesson_anchor: Mastra composite storage: memory, workflows, observability to different backends; ClickHouse recommended for observability at scale
parts.storage: composite: SQLite for memory, one JSON snapshot file per run id, an append-only NDJSON observability log
parts.exactness: snapshots compared with a type- and key-order-aware comparison (True vs 1, 2.0 vs 2, 2**64 + 1, -0.0, dict key order), and every snapshot file must parse as JSON; run ids with slashes, '..', a near-collision and 349 characters; messages with \r\n; events with ns integer timestamps and a \u2028 inside an attribute; across a close and reopen
traps: sort_keys in the snapshot
run id used as the file name (FileNotFoundError, or a file outside workflows/)
slashes replaced with underscores, colliding nightly/2026-11-02 with nightly_2026-11-02
percent-encoded or base64 file names, too long for the 349-character backfill run id
snapshots pickled instead of stored as JSON
runs() ordered by file name
ASCII-escaped log instead of readable UTF-8
log read with str.splitlines, which splits on \u2028
log truncated on reopen
empty run id accepted
inserts never committed, lost at close

parts.lesson_anchor: Where this pattern goes wrong: Perf-for-perf's-sake (overhead is not the bottleneck); Exercise 3 (does Agno's 2μs matter to your workload?); the speed targets matter with thousands of short-lived agents per second
parts.algorithm: Little's law per stage (in_flight = rate x service time, utilization = in_flight / workers), bottleneck with a stated tie rule, max sustainable rate, and the end-to-end share saved by a faster stage; all exact with Fraction
traps: bottleneck taken as the slowest stage or the one with the most requests in flight (a 2000 req/s fan-in where one-worker instantiation is the bottleneck)
Greek mu U+03BC and micro sign U+00B5
int(float(s) * 10**9) truncates 2.05 s; round() accepts 1.5ns
utilization exactly 1 counted as sustainable
workers_needed = ceil(in_flight) when in_flight is an integer
a tie broken by stage order instead of the longer service time
float utilization (0.1125 != Fraction(9, 80))
saving measured against the new total
max_rate derived from the current rate, dividing by zero at rate 0
zero service time, a negative rate or a '+' sign accepted

parts.lesson_anchor: Agno production path: stateless session-scoped FastAPI backend; Mastra server adapters (Express, Hono, Fastify, Koa); Build It: run an agent, stream the output, persist session
parts.wire_format: HTTP/1.1 chunked transfer encoding as raw bytes (hex size CRLF data CRLF, last chunk 0 CRLF CRLF), decided by the test's own chunk parser
traps: chunk size in characters instead of UTF-8 bytes
chunk size in decimal
chunk size written with hex() as 0x11
an empty token sent as a chunk ends the response early
whitespace-only tokens skipped as if empty
one lock for every session
no lock, or a new lock for every request
history read before the session lock
the reply buffered until the model finishes
lock acquired without try/finally, so aclose() leaves the session locked
the user turn stored before the reply completes
turns stored after the last chunk, lost when the client closes right after reading it
clarifying_questions: client closes after the last chunk

parts.lesson_anchor: Mastra's three primitives: Agents, Tools (Zod-typed), Workflows; workflow steps pass each output to the next step
traps: integer and number assignability reversed
an optional output given to a required input
an optional input field treated as required
a union destination split before a union source
a union source accepted when any member fits
array items not compared
strict objects not rejecting extra fields
nested flows unwrapped one level only
a nested flow's output taken from its first step
outer links checked before the links inside a nested flow, or the links inside it before the link into it
structure (empty or self-containing flows) checked only along the way, or emptiness only at the top
a reused sub-flow rejected as a cycle by a global visited set

deviations: Part 1 keeps the suggested shared-instance bug as an app that builds one Agent in __init__ and reuses it, the shape of code/main.py main(). The workflow trace, which the lesson's MastraWorkflow.run aliases, is already deep-copied in the starter: shared mutable objects are planted defects in 14/14 and 14/20 (and in 13/06), so here those assertions only guard the copy. The third defect comes from Mastra's Zod-typed tools instead: check_input walks the args rather than the schema that code/main.ts checkSchema walks. Part 3 adds latency_saving, so the 'does 2μs matter' question has a number. Part 5 reports the first mismatch with a JSON-path-like path and qualified leaf step names, and checks structure before links. The Mastra Model Router is not used anywhere, to avoid 13/21.
